quotes.text: ABRA draws its studies from three public collections, all accessed through TCIA
fields drawn from the dataset and per-study metadata (patient ID, study UID, series UID, slice ranges, ground-truth labels)

rationale: The packet names the data platform, datasets, cohort details, and per-task fields linking tasks back to records. It also reports task IDs/templates containing study and series identifiers, giving a route from tasks to source records.

quotes.text: LIDC-IDRI | Thoracic CT | 10 | 20 | 142 | CT (10), DX (8), CR (2), SEG (61), SR (61) | Armato et al. ...
Their usage was authorized via a data use agreement

rationale: Origin and licences are reported for the public TCIA datasets, and the packet also includes a consent/governance statement via a data use agreement. The note includes a repo MIT licence, but source-data terms are separately stated.

quotes.text: Patients | Studies | Series | Modalities (series) | Reference | License

rationale: S1 reports descriptive cohort statistics such as patients, studies, series, and modalities. A named target-population comparison appears only in S4 code comments, which does not count as reporting.

searched: S1 paper and appendix, S2 README/docs, S3 release notes, S4 code, S5 agent-visible prompts/tool descriptions. The packet does not report dedicated unsafe-output tests or bias tests on public reporting surfaces.

quotes.text: labels reside in an independent evaluation service disconnected from the agent sandbox with no network route

rationale: The paper reports a developer-side isolation control for labels. It does not report a measured contamination check; a general concern sentence is insufficient for full credit.

quotes.text: ground truth is isolated from runtime agent access
with no network route, and the repository does not publish them

rationale: The paper states runtime isolation from ground truth and names mechanisms: independent evaluation service, no network route, and unpublished labels.

quotes.text: database snapshot, the software image and the simulated-patient language model are all pinned to fixed versions
no external service is called at evaluation time other than the model under test

rationale: S1 explicitly states pinned data, software, and simulator/judge model state, with no live external service except the evaluated model.

searched: S1 paper and appendix, S2 README/docs, S3 release notes, S4 code, S5 agent-visible prompts/tool descriptions. Scripted reference-solution evidence appears only in S4 comments, which do not count as reporting.

quotes.text: checks both the intended state changes and that all other records remain unchanged

rationale: Tasks change viewer or annotation state, so NA does not apply. S1 reports that the grader checks both intended changes and unchanged records.

quotes.text: Turn efficiency penalises aimless long trajectories

rationale: The benchmark gives design arguments that trivial trajectories are discouraged through redundancy and turn-efficiency penalties. It does not report an empirical random or trivial-agent success rate.
searched: S1 paper and appendix, S2 README/docs, S3 release notes, S4 code, S5 agent-visible prompts/tool descriptions. No do-nothing or random-agent score is reported.

quotes.text: validated the automatic evaluator on 200 outputs labelled by two physicians
agreement was 94%, with a false-positive rate of 3% and a false-negative rate of 8%

rationale: S1 reports benchmark-specific evaluator validation on its own outputs, including agreement and per-class error figures.

quotes.text: Every run applies temperature 0 with a fixed seed
the policy of executing each task three times

rationale: S1 reports temperature 0 with a fixed seed and a repeated-run policy. Another S1 sentence says results came from a single run, but contradiction flags only apply to S4/S5 against S1-S3.

quotes.text: We report 95% confidence intervals computed by bootstrapping over tasks

rationale: S1 reports confidence intervals for results using bootstrapping. This satisfies the CI criterion for model comparisons.

quotes.text: Our results were obtained from a single run of each model.
Every run applies temperature 0 with a fixed seed.

rationale: The packet reports the run count per task behind results and decoding/seed controls. It does not state whether runs are independent.

quotes.text: 95% confidence intervals computed by bootstrapping over tasks
where several tasks share a patient, we resample patients instead to account for clustering

rationale: S1 reports CIs, names the resampling unit, and addresses clustering by patient. All three elements are present.

quotes.text: reports `pass^k` (probability that ALL k repeats of a task succeed)
--workers 4 --repeats 8

rationale: The README reports a pass^k-style all-runs reliability metric and gives a repeat count example. It does not report action-sequence or final-state agreement across reruns.

quotes.text: API snapshots: GPT-5.4 ( gpt-5.4-2026-03-05 )
temperature 0 and 2,048-token output ceiling. All reported results match harness version v1.2.0.

rationale: S1 reports provider snapshot identifiers, decoding parameters, and the harness version for reported results. Although S4 contains generic config names, the reported S1 pinning satisfies the checklist item.

quotes.text: Each tool is presented as a typed JSON function-calling schema
Actions in ABRA fall into three classes: navigation and display , segmentation , and reporting

rationale: The paper reports machine-readable tool schemas and classifies actions by side effect. S5 tool descriptions also tell the agent which calls set, select, submit, or query state. Error/failure return semantics are not documented on S1-S3.

quotes.text: We ran conformance tests confirming that each tool behaves as documented.
Two tools are simulated stubs that return fixed placeholder responses

rationale: S1 reports conformance tests and discloses simulated stub tools. The simulated oracle tools are also described to agents in S5 as external model queries with structured returns.

quotes.text: Segmentation actions deposit region-of-interest annotations in pixel coordinates
Episodes run in isolated browser contexts
Extraneous calls not present in T_ref incur a small redundancy penalty

rationale: The benchmark has write actions, so NA does not apply. S1 identifies mutating actions, says episodes are sandboxed in isolated browser contexts, and reports penalties for extraneous calls; S5 also marks terminal submission actions and state-changing tools.

quotes.text: automatic scorers that run on the controller’s trajectory logs
validated the automatic evaluator on 200 outputs labelled by two physicians

rationale: S1 names grader inputs as trajectory logs and state/outcome signals, and explains outcome scoring by task type. Validation on 200 physician-labelled outputs reports agreement and false-positive/false-negative rates.

quotes.text: labels reside in an independent evaluation service disconnected from the agent sandbox with no network route
the repository does not publish them

rationale: The packet reports controls on leakage from ground truth to the agent and states labels are not public. It does not report a canary or provenance marker on released tasks.

quotes.text: per-task-type Planning, Execution, and Outcome scores across the eight ABRA task types
Accuracy is reported by task family (diagnosis, ordering, documentation) and by patient subgroup (sex, race)
with case counts displayed for every slice in the tables

rationale: S1 reports results by task type and includes n values in the task-type table. It also states subgroup reporting by sex and race with case counts.

quotes.text: genuine, de-identified entries sourced from a hospital database
data use agreement that mandated credentialed access and de-identification compliant with the safe harbour method
distributed under terms distinct from the MIT code licence

rationale: S1 states the environment records are real and de-identified, gives governance through DUA and safe-harbour de-identification, and separates data terms from the code licence.
